title: Endolift vs Dermal Fillers: Which Lifting Treatment Is Right for You?
description: Compare Endolift laser skin tightening with dermal fillers. Learn which non-surgical lifting treatment suits your goals and budget in Leicester.
excerpt: Two popular non-surgical options for facial rejuvenation: Endolift and dermal fillers. We break down the key differences, costs, and results to help you choose.
author: Dr Gunjan Bedi
heroImageAlt: Comparison of Endolift laser and dermal filler results for face lifting
content:
## Introduction

When it comes to non-surgical facial rejuvenation, two treatments stand out: **Endolift** and **dermal fillers**. Both can address sagging skin, volume loss, and fine lines, but they work in fundamentally different ways.

If you're considering a lifting treatment in Leicester, understanding the differences between these two approaches will help you make an informed decision that aligns with your goals and budget.

## What Is Endolift?

Endolift is a **laser-based skin tightening treatment** that works from the inside out. A thin laser fibre is gently inserted beneath the skin's surface, where it:

- **Melts small fat deposits** for subtle contouring
- **Stimulates collagen production** through controlled heat
- **Contracts skin fibres** immediately, with continued improvement over months

**Best for:** Overall skin tightening, sagging skin, jowls, double chin, and gradual, natural-looking results.

## What Are Dermal Fillers?

Dermal fillers are **injectable gels** that instantly restore volume by filling lines and folds. Common fillers include:

- Hyaluronic acid fillers (e.g., Juvederm, Restylane)
- Biostimulating fillers (e.g., Profhilo, polynucleotides)

**Best for:** Targeted volume restoration, nasolabial folds, thin lips, and immediate results.

## Head-to-Head Comparison

| Feature | Endolift | Dermal Fillers |
|---------|----------|----------------|
| **How It Works** | Laser-induced collagen stimulation | Volume restoration |
| **Results Timeline** | Progressive (3-6 months) | Immediate (24-48 hours) |
| **Longevity** | 2-3 years | 6-18 months (varies) |
| **Downtime** | 1-3 days | None to minimal |
| **Cost Range** | £1,500-3,000+ | £300-800 per syringe |
| **Best for** | Skin tightening, overall lift | Volume loss, specific areas |
| **Pain Level** | Mild discomfort | Minimal (numbing gel applied) |

## Key Differences Explained

### Treatment Mechanism

**Endolift** addresses the root cause of sagging: loss of skin elasticity. By stimulating new collagen, it rebuilds your skin's structural support.

**Fillers** work on the surface, adding volume to smooth lines and restore fullness in specific areas.

### Timeline & Patience

With **Endolift**, patience pays off. Visible results appear within 4-8 weeks, with full results at 6 months. Many patients report continued subtle improvements for up to 9 months.

**Fillers** offer instant gratification—results are visible within hours of injection.

### Cost Considerations

A single Endolift treatment (£1,500-3,000) may seem expensive upfront, but the 2-3 year longevity makes it cost-effective long-term.

Fillers require regular touch-ups every 6-18 months, depending on the product. A full-face treatment with multiple syringes can be £1,200-2,000 annually.

## Which Treatment Is Right for You?

### Choose **Endolift** if you:

✓ Have noticeable skin sagging or laxity  
✓ Want a natural-looking, gradual transformation  
✓ Prefer fewer touch-ups long-term  
✓ Are willing to wait 6 months for optimal results  
✓ Want to address jowls, neck sagging, or double chin  

### Choose **Dermal Fillers** if you:

✓ Want immediate results  
✓ Have minimal downtime requirements  
✓ Prefer to target specific lines or lips  
✓ Want to test results before committing to more invasive options  
✓ Don't mind regular maintenance appointments  

## The Best Approach: Combination Therapy

Many of our patients at The One Clinic achieve optimal results by **combining both treatments**:

1. **Endolift** for overall skin tightening and collagen induction
2. **Fillers** to address specific volume loss in high-impact areas (lips, nasolabial folds)

This dual approach maximizes lifting, restores youth, and extends results.

## Why Choose The One Clinic?

At The One Clinic in Leicester, our doctors assess your unique skin concerns and recommend the best treatment—whether that's Endolift, fillers, or a combination approach.

**We offer:**
- Expert consultations with GMC-registered doctors
- Personalised treatment plans
- Cutting-edge technology in a purpose-built clinic
- Natural, subtle results
- Minimal downtime options

## Next Steps

If you're torn between Endolift and dermal fillers, book a consultation with our team. We'll assess your skin, discuss your goals, and recommend the best option for you—or suggest a combination approach.

**Ready to explore your options?** [Book a consultation with The One Clinic today](/contact).

---

## FAQs

**Q: Can I do Endolift and fillers in the same session?**  
A: Yes, many patients combine both treatments on the same day or with a few weeks between appointments.

**Q: Will Endolift results last longer than fillers?**  
A: Yes. Endolift typically lasts 2-3 years, while fillers last 6-18 months depending on the product and area treated.

**Q: Is Endolift painful?**  
A: Endolift involves mild discomfort but is performed under local anaesthetic, so pain is minimal.

**Q: Can I combine Endolift with other treatments?**  
A: Absolutely. Many patients pair it with our Morpheus8 radiofrequency treatment or biostimulating fillers like Profhilo for enhanced results.

title: 5 Signs Your Skin Needs Professional Treatment (and What The One Clinic Offers)
description: Discover the key indicators that your skin would benefit from professional aesthetic treatment. From fine lines to hyperpigmentation, learn when to seek help.
excerpt: Your skin sends signals when it needs a little extra care. Here are five clear signs that professional treatment could transform your complexion.
author: Dr Sumit Virmani
heroImageAlt: Woman examining her skin for signs of aging and damage
content:
## Introduction

Your skin is constantly evolving. While some changes are purely cosmetic, others may signal that your skin is struggling and could benefit from professional intervention.

At The One Clinic, we assess thousands of patients each year. Here are the five most common signs we see that indicate it's time to explore professional skin treatments.

## Sign 1: Persistent Fine Lines and Wrinkles That Don't Fade

**What to look for:**
- Lines around your eyes (crow's feet) that are visible even when your face is relaxed
- Forehead lines that don't smooth out
- Marionette lines around your mouth that deepened over time

**Why it happens:**  
Fine lines result from repeated facial expressions, sun damage, and natural collagen loss (we lose about 1% of collagen annually after age 30).

**What we recommend:**  
- **Morpheus8**: Radiofrequency micro-needling for deeper collagen induction
- **Laser resurfacing**: Removes damaged layers and stimulates new skin growth
- **Dermal fillers**: For targeted, immediate smoothing of expression lines

---

## Sign 2: Uneven Skin Tone and Stubborn Hyperpigmentation

**What to look for:**
- Dark patches or spots that don't fade with sunscreen
- Freckles that have darkened or multiplied
- Overall dull, blotchy complexion despite good skincare
- Sun damage or melasma that covers large areas

**Why it happens:**  
UV exposure, hormonal changes, and inflammation trigger melanin overproduction. Once hyperpigmentation sets in, topical creams often can't penetrate deeply enough to address it.

**What we recommend:**  
- **Lumecca IPL**: Targets pigmentation at the source with intense pulsed light
- **Laser resurfacing**: Removes pigmented layers and reveals fresh skin beneath
- **Chemical peels**: Accelerates skin turnover to fade discoloration

---

## Sign 3: Sagging Skin or Loss of Definition in the Jawline and Neck

**What to look for:**
- Sagging cheeks or jowls that make your face appear heavier
- Loss of definition along your jawline
- Crepey skin on the neck or décolletage
- A "tired" appearance even when well-rested

**Why it happens:**  
Collagen and elastin breakdown, combined with facial fat descent, creates visible sagging. Gravity and repeated movements accelerate this process over time.

**What we recommend:**  
- **Endolift**: Non-surgical laser lifting with minimal downtime
- **Morpheus8**: Tightens loose skin through radiofrequency stimulation
- **Biostimulating fillers** (Profhilo): Hydrate and firm the skin from within

---

## Sign 4: Persistent Acne, Enlarged Pores, or Rough Texture

**What to look for:**
- Adult acne that doesn't respond to over-the-counter treatments
- Visibly enlarged pores that trap dirt and oil
- Bumpy or uneven skin texture despite good skincare
- Frequent breakouts in the same areas

**Why it happens:**  
Excess oil production, bacterial colonization, and inflammation require professional intervention. Over-the-counter products often can't reach the deeper layers of skin where acne starts.

**What we recommend:**  
- **HydraFacial**: Deep extraction and hydration in a single appointment
- **Chemical peels**: Dissolve debris and unclog pores
- **Laser resurfacing**: Targets bacteria and normalizes oil production
- **Professional facials**: Customized treatments based on your skin type

---

## Sign 5: Dark Circles, Under-Eye Bags, or Loss of Volume

**What to look for:**
- Persistent dark circles that don't fade with sleep or makeup
- Puffy bags under your eyes
- Hollowness under your eyes that makes you look tired
- Fine lines and crepey skin around the orbital area

**Why it happens:**  
The under-eye area is thinner and more delicate. Volume loss, pigmentation, and loose skin all contribute to a tired appearance.

**What we recommend:**  
- **Dermal fillers**: Instant volume restoration under the eyes
- **Non-surgical blepharoplasty**: Tightens the under-eye area without surgery
- **Laser resurfacing**: Stimulates collagen and improves dark circles
- **Profhilo**: Hydrates and firms delicate under-eye skin

---

## When Should You Seek Professional Help?

You don't need to wait for multiple signs to appear. Consider professional treatment if:

✓ Your skin concern affects your confidence  
✓ Over-the-counter products haven't worked after 12 weeks  
✓ You want to prevent further damage  
✓ You're ready for visible, lasting results  
✓ A skin condition is causing physical discomfort  

## The Consultation Advantage

The best first step is always a **professional skin consultation**. At The One Clinic:

- Our doctors assess your skin type, concerns, and goals
- We recommend treatments backed by clinical evidence
- We explain realistic timelines and costs
- We customise a plan that fits your budget and lifestyle

Many patients combine treatments for optimal results. For example, addressing hyperpigmentation with Lumecca IPL, then improving texture with a HydraFacial, then refreshing with a chemical peel.

## Next Steps

If you've noticed any of these five signs, don't wait years hoping they'll fade. Professional treatment can deliver dramatic improvements in weeks.

**Book a consultation with The One Clinic today.** Our doctors will assess your skin and recommend the best path forward—whether that's a single treatment or a customised skin programme.

[Schedule your free skin consultation](/contact)

---

## FAQs

**Q: Is it ever too late to treat skin damage?**  
A: No. Advanced technologies can improve even long-standing concerns. Consistency and professional guidance matter most.

**Q: Can I combine multiple treatments?**  
A: Yes. Many patients benefit from a layered approach (e.g., Lumecca IPL + HydraFacial + chemical peel over several weeks).

**Q: How long do results last?**  
A: It depends on the treatment. Some results are immediate (fillers), while others improve gradually (laser resurfacing). Maintenance varies.

**Q: Is professional skincare expensive?**  
A: Not compared to years of ineffective over-the-counter products. Plus, professional treatments deliver visible results in fewer sessions.

title: Complete Post-Treatment Care Guide: What to Do After Your Aesthetic Procedure
description: Essential aftercare tips for laser, filler, and injectables. Learn how to maximise results and minimise downtime after your aesthetic treatment.
excerpt: Your treatment doesn't end when you leave the clinic. Proper aftercare is crucial for optimal results. Here's everything you need to know.
author: Dr Gunjan Bedi
content:
## Introduction

You've booked your aesthetic treatment and completed the appointment. Now comes the critical phase: **aftercare**.

The first 24-72 hours following your treatment are crucial. What you do—and don't do—during this window directly impacts your results, downtime duration, and risk of complications.

This guide covers aftercare for the most popular treatments at The One Clinic.

## Universal Aftercare Rules (All Treatments)

Regardless of which treatment you've had, follow these core principles:

### 1. **Avoid Heat for 48 Hours**
- No hot showers or baths
- No saunas, steam rooms, or hot tubs
- No intense exercise or sweat-inducing activities
- No direct sunlight

**Why:** Heat dilates blood vessels and increases inflammation, swelling, and bruising.

### 2. **Keep Your Hands Off Your Face**
- Don't touch, rub, or scratch the treated area
- Avoid makeup for at least 24 hours (some treatments 48 hours)
- Don't apply other skincare products except those recommended by your doctor

**Why:** Your skin barrier is compromised post-treatment. Contact introduces bacteria and can cause infection or disrupted healing.

### 3. **Stay Hydrated**
- Drink 2-3 litres of water daily
- Hydrated skin heals faster and shows better results

### 4. **Sleep with Your Head Elevated**
- Use 2-3 pillows to reduce fluid pooling
- This minimises swelling, especially after injectables or laser treatments

### 5. **Use SPF 50+ Daily**
- Sun exposure can cause permanent pigmentation and damage new skin
- Apply sunscreen every 2 hours if outdoors

---

## Treatment-Specific Aftercare

### **Laser Resurfacing** (Lumecca, Laser Genesis, CO₂)

**First 24 hours:**
- Expect redness, mild swelling, and possible oozing
- Apply ice packs (10 minutes on, 10 minutes off) for the first 6 hours
- Use prescribed healing ointment every 2-3 hours
- Keep skin clean and dry

**Days 2-7:**
- Redness peaks around day 2-3
- Mild peeling and flaking begin
- Continue ointment application; don't pick at peeling skin
- Use gentle cleanser (no scrubbing)
- Apply broad-spectrum SPF 50+ daily

**Weeks 2-4:**
- Peeling subsides; skin looks fresher
- Continue sun protection religiously
- Introduce gentle moisturiser and basic skincare

**Timeline:** Redness fades by week 3; full results at 2-3 months.

### **Morpheus8** (Radiofrequency Micro-needling)

**First 24 hours:**
- Expect redness, mild warmth, and minimal swelling
- Ice packs reduce inflammation
- Avoid makeup and active products

**Days 2-5:**
- Redness fades significantly
- Skin may feel slightly sensitive
- Continue SPF 50+
- Can resume light exercise by day 3

**Weeks 2-8:**
- Collagen remodelling occurs beneath the surface
- Results gradually improve
- Avoid intense sun exposure

**Timeline:** Visible results by week 4; optimal results at 8 weeks. Results continue improving for up to 3 months.

### **Dermal Fillers & Injectables** (Profhilo, Juvederm, Restylane)

**First 24 hours:**
- Expect mild swelling, redness, and possible bruising
- Sleep elevated to reduce swelling
- Apply ice for 10 minutes per hour (first 6 hours only)
- Avoid makeup if possible

**Days 2-7:**
- Swelling peaks around day 2-3, then subsides
- Bruising may worsen before improving (use makeup to cover)
- Avoid massage or pressure on the treated area
- No intense exercise or hot activities

**Week 2+:**
- Swelling resolves
- Results stabilise
- Bruising fades (vitamin K cream can speed this)

**Timeline:** Initial results visible within 24 hours; full results at 2 weeks.

### **Chemical Peels** (TCA, Salicylic Acid)

**First 24-48 hours:**
- Expect visible peeling or crusting (depends on peel strength)
- Use prescribed post-peel balm or moisturiser
- Avoid water contact initially (follow your doctor's specific timeline)
- No makeup

**Days 3-7:**
- Heavy peeling; don't pick or force peeling
- Use gentle cleanser, warm (not hot) water
- Moisturise frequently
- SPF 50+ every 2 hours

**Weeks 2-4:**
- Peeling subsides; new skin is fresh and glowing
- Continue SPF diligently
- Introduce gentle serums or light treatments only

**Timeline:** Redness resolves by week 2; results improve for up to 3 months.

### **HydraFacial**

**Immediately & First 24 Hours:**
- No downtime; can resume normal activities
- Skin may feel slightly warm or flushed
- Avoid makeup for 2-4 hours
- Use gentle cleanser that evening

**First Week:**
- Skin is more receptive to serums and treatments
- Hydration peaks; skin looks plump and glowing
- Continue with your regular skincare routine
- Use SPF during the day

**Timeline:** Results visible immediately; benefits last 5-7 days. Recommend monthly treatments for maintenance.

---

## What to Avoid After Treatment

| Activity | Why | Duration |
|----------|-----|----------|
| Hot baths/showers | Increases inflammation | 48 hours |
| Exercise/sweating | Risk of infection; increases swelling | 48-72 hours |
| Makeup | Can introduce bacteria | 24-48 hours |
| Skincare actives (retinol, AHA, BHA) | Over-irritates treated skin | 1 week |
| Alcohol | Thins blood; increases bruising | 24-48 hours |
| Intense sun exposure | Risk of pigmentation damage | 2 weeks |
| Facials or other treatments | Can compound irritation | 2 weeks |
| Touching/rubbing the area | Risk of infection or scarring | 1 week |

---

## Signs Something Is Wrong

Most side effects are normal and temporary. However, **contact your doctor immediately if you experience:**

⚠️ Severe pain or swelling that worsens after day 3  
⚠️ Signs of infection (pus, excessive warmth, fever)  
⚠️ Severe or spreading rash  
⚠️ Blistering or severe burns (laser treatments)  
⚠️ Vision changes or eye swelling (eye area treatments)  
⚠️ Asymmetrical results 1 week after injectables  

---

## Maximise Your Results: The 4-Week Protocol

**Week 1:** Healing phase—focus on protection and gentle care  
**Week 2:** Enhancement phase—introduce supporting skincare (serums, moisturiser)  
**Week 3:** Maintenance phase—consistent SPF, gentle routine  
**Week 4:** Results evaluation—book follow-up if needed  

---

## When Can You Resume Normal Activities?

- **Light exercise:** Day 2-3 post-treatment
- **Intense exercise:** Day 5-7 (depending on treatment)
- **Makeup:** 24-48 hours
- **Skincare actives:** 1 week
- **Sun exposure:** Avoid for 2 weeks; then SPF 50+
- **Next aesthetic treatment:** 2 weeks minimum

---

## Questions About Your Aftercare?

Every treatment and patient is unique. If you're unsure whether an activity is safe post-treatment, **contact The One Clinic** before doing it.

We provide detailed aftercare instructions with every treatment, and our team is available to answer questions during your recovery.

**Have more questions? [Contact us](/contact) or book a post-treatment check-in appointment.**

---

## Key Takeaway

**Aftercare is not optional—it's part of your treatment.** The 24-72 hours following your appointment set the tone for your results. Follow these guidelines, and you'll enjoy faster healing, better results, and minimal complications.

Your investment in professional treatment deserves proper aftercare. You've got this!
